The scaffold’s per-pair matrix records the exact subset of these ranges supporting each FR pair.

## Seam-controlled refusals

The scaffold does not re-mint:

- Functional-analysis-owned Fourier transforms, Schwartz and tempered-distribution theory, Plancherel, the Hilbert-space Fourier-series foundation, basic Poisson summation, basic Heisenberg uncertainty, or the existing Wiener lemma.
- Measure-theory-owned Hardy–Littlewood maximal and differentiation theorems, Marcinkiewicz interpolation, or Riesz–Thorin interpolation, under subjects-01 ruling R-6.
- PDE-owned Sobolev definitions and embeddings; FR supplies only Fourier characterisations.
- RG-owned Haar existence or noncommutative unitary representation theory.
- Complex-analysis-owned holomorphic Hardy spaces and BMOA.
- A Strichartz theorem or invented PDE page identifier.

The fifteen pre-existing item-id overlaps are intentional seam transfers or reserved reuse: seven from functional analysis and eight generic Calderón–Zygmund items from PDE. No proposed page-id collision was found.

## Recorded blockers

- FR-14/FR-15 retain `RG-?` for Haar existence and uniqueness because the concurrent RG scaffold supplied no stable relative label.
- The existing PDE scaffold has no Strichartz page. FR-13 records the interface without fabricating one.

Both blockers were documented in the scaffold without prompting or expanding ownership.
